profile.reading:
CloudHQ LC13 sits at 21605 Lockridge Road, Ashburn, Virginia, one of fourteen numbered buildings on CloudHQ's LC Campus, which the company's own current campus page places directly off Loudoun County Parkway "in the heart of Ashburn," describing the site as sitting amid "the densest concentration of fiber in the world." CloudHQ states the full LC Campus totals roughly 8.5 million square feet and 1,256 megawatts of total critical IT load across its fourteen data centers, with 756 megawatts currently available; this is a campus-wide total that CloudHQ does not break out by individual building, and no third-party aggregator figure specific to LC13 was found either. CloudHQ was founded in 2016 by Hossein Fateh, who also founded QTS Realty Trust and, per CloudHQ's own materials, was the first person in the United States to obtain an IRS ruling allowing data center income to qualify for real estate investment trust tax treatment. CloudHQ is privately held through the Fateh Family Office, with regional headquarters in Washington DC, London, and Singapore, and states a company-wide net-zero emissions target by 2040, along with generator fuel supplied by HVO biodiesel "wherever it is reliably available" and a stated goal of net biodiversity gain on all new campuses. CloudHQ markets a "campus within a campus" concept at LC, allowing customers to take multiple LC-numbered buildings as one contiguous deployment. CloudHQ does not name a power utility for the LC Campus on its current site; Dominion Energy is the dominant electric utility across Loudoun County as a matter of public record.

Loudoun County's Ashburn corridor is the largest concentration of data center capacity in the world, hosting dozens of competing hyperscale and colocation operators within a few miles of CloudHQ's LC Campus. CloudHQ's global portfolio spans 23 campuses and more than 30 million square feet across six countries, with more than 1,380 megawatts of critical IT load already contracted company-wide and over 6,000 megawatts of further expansion potential, figures CloudHQ discloses on its own homepage alongside a stated 5.2-gigawatt global data center inventory.
profile.capacity_note: not published by the operator at the building level. Per CloudHQs own current page for the LC Campus (tier-1 operator source, https://cloudhq.com/campus/lc-campus/), this campus is in the heart of Ashburn, Virginia, directly off Loudoun County Parkway, and totals about 8.5 million square feet and 1,256 MW of total critical IT load across fourteen data centers, with 756 MW available critical load, as of this sessions retrieval. Because this is a fourteen-building campus total, it is not applied to any individual rows critical_it_mw.

Facility specific seeding pass 2026-09-02, batch 38 (CloudHQ VA missing-address campaign): preferred a distinguishing datacenterHawk address over a Baxtel figure shared with a neighboring row, refreshed company history from the operators own about and founder pages, flagged a second CloudHQ name collision on Wikipedia not present in a prior sessions notes. research_status remains complete.

[batch narration moved out of reading 2026-09-02] CloudHQ, the data center operator, was established in 2016 by Hossein Fateh, per the operators own current about page (cloudhq.com/about/) fetched fresh this session. Fateh previously served as CEO and co-founder of DuPont Fabros Technology, a data center company that sold for 7.8 billion dollars in 2017, and has built and operated more than 700 MW of data center capacity across his career, per CloudHQs own founder page (cloudhq.com/learn-about-our-founder/), also fetched fresh this session. CloudHQ operates as part of the Fateh Family Office, alongside affiliated companies CloudCapital, WindHQ, and Dalian Development, per the operators own about page. The company maintains three regional headquarters, a global headquarters in Washington DC, an EMEA headquarters in London, and an APAC headquarters in Singapore. Per the operators own current about page, CloudHQ now describes 23 global campuses, more than 1,380 MW of contracted critical IT load with more than 6,000 MW of expansion potential, more than 30 million square feet of global data center portfolio, and more than 330 employees. A prior research pass on these rows had already flagged that the domain cloudhq.net resolves to an unrelated Google Workspace and Gmail backup software company, not this data center operator, and correctly redirected to cloudhq.com. This session found a second, separate name collision worth flagging for a future researcher: the Wikipedia article at en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CloudHQ describes yet another different, unrelated company, a cloud data synchronization tool for Google Workspace founded in 2011 by Senad Dizdar and based in San Francisco, not this Ashburn and Manassas Virginia data center operator founded by Hossein Fateh. That Wikipedia article was checked this session and found not to apply, so it is not used or cited as a source here, and no Wikipedia sourced company history is included in this reading. This specific row, LC13, has conflicting aggregator sourcing. Baxtels own dedicated LC13 page gives 22141 Loudoun County Pkwy, Ashburn, the identical figure Baxtel separately assigns to neighboring LC14, so it does not distinguish this row from LC14. DatacenterHawks dedicated LC13 listing instead gives 21605 Lockridge Road, Northern Virginia, a genuinely distinct street, close to but not identical to this registrys LC5 row at 21615 Lockridge Rd. Because the datacenterHawk figure is distinguishing and plausibly places LC13 near its Lockridge Road neighbor LC5 rather than colliding with LC14, it is preferred here, with Baxtels competing, shared figure flagged rather than silently dropped.

reading.body:
CloudHQ LC13 is one building in a fourteen-building campus in Ashburn, Virginia that totals 1,256 MW of critical IT load with 756 MW available for new tenants. The operator does not publish capacity at the individual building level. At 40 kW per rack, a common AI training density, 756 MW of available IT load across the entire LC campus represents roughly 18,900 racks, though this figure covers all fourteen buildings and cannot be attributed to LC13 alone.

The LC campus sits in Loudoun County, the state's dominant data center cluster and home to 1,375 MW of published capacity across 23 facilities. This campus ranks twenty-fourth by published megawattage in Virginia but represents a substantial share of the state's AI-ready infrastructure as part of a single operator's interconnected footprint. Virginia's 326 mapped data centers mostly publish no capacity figures, so published capacity concentrates among a small number of operators at major sites.

The campus location in Ashburn places it within reach of major internet exchange points and established fiber corridors serving hyperscale cloud providers. No certifications or power procurement details are published for this building or campus. Operator background and expansion plans are not relevant to whether this campus matters to AI scaling, but the unpublished availability of 756 MW across fourteen buildings suggests active buildout capacity that is not yet committed to tenants.
